resources.string: The phone\'s screen is on the TV, with its sound, a few seconds behind.
The phone\'s screen, with its sound, on an Apple TV or a TV with AirPlay. A few seconds behind: good for apps and video, not fast games.
No AirPlay TVs found. Check the TV is on and on the same Wi-Fi.
That code didn\'t match. Type the new one.
%1$s didn\'t allow it. On an Apple TV, set AirPlay\'s Allow Access to everyone on the same network, then try again.
Looking for TVs on this Wi-Fi…
Starting on %1$s… Allow the screen to be shared if asked.
The phone\'s screen is on the TV, with its sound. Tap an app below to put it on the TV alone.
Connecting to %1$s… Accept on the TV if it asks.
The phone\'s screen, with its sound, on a TV or PC that takes Miracast (LG Screen Share, Samsung Screen Mirroring, Windows), with no app on the TV.
Couldn\'t connect to %1$s. Accept the request on the TV if it asks, then try again.
No screens found. Turn on Screen Share (or Screen Mirroring) on the TV, then look again.
This phone\'s Android doesn\'t offer Miracast.
Pairing PINs and requests to stream come as notifications.
Open Moonlight on your TV or PC: it lists this phone. Pick it, then enter the PIN this phone shows.
Streaming shares the screen and passes on Moonlight\'s controls through it.
Moonlight lists every app on the phone besides your games, each opening on a screen of its own. Off: only the apps you long-press in the Streaming app.

Keeps the phone listed in Moonlight while streaming is off, so you don\'t need Wake (some Moonlight apps, like the one for LG webOS, send their Wake where the phone can\'t hear it). Picking a game turns streaming on. Pair once with streaming on first.
Don\'t ask again for this device
It wants to stream from this phone.
It wants to play %1$s from this phone.
%1$s is visible in Moonlight on this network.
Send keyboards, mice and controllers to the stream
Keyboards, mice and controllers connected by USB or Bluetooth control what\'s streamed instead of the phone. They go back to the phone when the stream ends.
Adds the phone\'s screen to Moonlight\'s list, to show whatever is on it.
Show the phone\'s screen in Moonlight

The Moonlight client gets the stream\'s sound whatever this is set to. Media sound off turns the phone\'s media volume to nothing while a stream plays; All sounds off also silences notifications, the ringer and the phone\'s own sounds (calls and messages vibrate). Alarms still sound. Everything goes back as it was when the stream ends.
Automatic streams at the resolution set in Moonlight on the client, 4K included. Choosing a size runs what\'s streamed at that size and lets the client scale it up, which is easier on the phone.

Mirror shows the phone\'s screen on the Moonlight client. Separate screen runs the app or game on its own screen for the client and leaves the phone free; the Games app shows it on the phone and sends your keys, touches and placed keys to it. Android desktop does the same with Android 16\'s desktop, switching desktop windowing on for you (a restart may be needed the first time). You can switch between them from the streaming notification.

Lists the phone in Moonlight on any device on the same network. Pair with the PIN Moonlight shows: the phone\'s screen, Android\'s desktop and your games appear there, XCloud games included. Moonlight\'s Wake starts streaming on the phone if it\'s off.
Moonlight lists your Termux:Widget scripts too: picking one runs it and shows Termux on the TV. Needs Termux and the permission to run commands in it.
%1$d paired. Each will need the PIN again.
Every app is in Moonlight\'s list already. To list only the ones you pick, turn off Every app in Moonlight in ⚙
Nothing is streaming yet: start streaming from Moonlight, or set up your TV in streaming\'s settings to start apps on it from here
Tap an app to open it on the TV while you stream. Long-press one to list it in Moonlight too.
Tap an app to open it on the TV while you stream. Moonlight lists every app (see ⚙).
On your TV or PC, open Moonlight and pick this phone. %1$s there opens this page on the TV, to pick an app.
Moonlight can\'t find the phone until it\'s on.
Apps you tap here open on the TV.
Find a Moonlight client on the Wi-Fi (LG webOS for now). Flux Streaming can then turn it on and open Moonlight straight into a game you pick on the phone.
%1$s: picking a game while streaming can stream it there. Tap to find it again or forget it.
Moonlight couldn\'t be opened on %1$s. Is Moonlight installed there?
Looking for Moonlight clients on the Wi-Fi…

Ask each time: opening a game while streaming asks whether to stream it to the Moonlight client (turned on, Moonlight opened straight into the game) or play it on the phone. With streaming off, games play on the phone.
Flux Streaming turns this Moonlight client on and opens Moonlight on it into the game you pick. For turning it on, it needs Turn on via Wi-Fi (or Mobile TV On) in its settings.
%1$s didn\'t answer. Turn it on, or turn on Turn on via Wi-Fi (Mobile TV On) in its settings.
No Moonlight client found. It needs to be on and on the same Wi-Fi (LG webOS for now).
Turn the TV off when the stream ends
When a stream to this TV ends and no other starts within 20 seconds, the TV is turned off.
%1$s didn\'t allow Flux Streaming. Accept it there when asked.
%1$s is set up. Pair Moonlight on it with this phone once, if you haven\'t.
Couldn\'t set up %1$s. Check it\'s on, then try again.
Volume buttons change the TV\'s volume

While streaming to this TV, the phone\'s volume buttons turn it up or down, with the accessibility helper on. In a game, where they\'re the triggers, hold SYM with them. The TV may ask once to allow it.

Moonlight on a TV or PC streams from the phone as it would from a PC (the GameStream protocol, as Sunshine answers it). Sound is coded with Concentus (Opus in Java); AirPlay pairs with Bouncy Castle, after pyatv’s notes on the protocol.
